findings.message: D301 (SMA6T6V7AY): voltage 4.2 vs rating 5 (84%) between TAP0 and TAP1 — above 80% derating
findings.waived_by: designer: TVS stand-off by design sits just above the working voltage: VRWM is itself the working-voltage rating (leakage specified at VRWM: 20 uA, 1 uA, 10 nA). An 80 % derating would push the clamp above what it protects (LT8584 VIN 9 V, C6kk/D1 100 V, ISO7721 6 V).

findings.message: external net TAP0_IN declares threat 'reverse_polarity' but has no diode/mosfet on it
findings.waived_by: designer: Reversed or swapped taps are handled by crowbar, not blocking: the unidirectional TVS D3kk conducts forward on reversal and the board fuse F1tt opens (H-8, F-6). A series diode would add 0.5 V x 2.5 A per tap and halve the efficiency budget. The framework counts only diode/MOSFET categories.

findings.message: external power net iso/VIO_ISO reaches the board without a fuse/PTC on it
findings.waived_by: designer: VIO_ISO is the host's logic supply into U5 side 2 only (<= 4 mA, ISO7721 SLLSEP3G); the host port limits it. A fuse would not open at these currents.

findings.message: Q-1 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Pack range: confirm 13-16S at <= 60 V. Above 60 V leaves ES1/SELV; below 13S the transformer's 30 V output minimum is not met (NA6252-AL would be needed).
Q-2 is BLOCKING and unanswered: BMS interaction: disable the pack BMS's bleed balancing? Is a CAN/RS-485 link required?
Q-3 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Is the battery isolated from mains by the inverter? If so the user barrier can be functional.
Q-4 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Harness: accept 18 AWG <= 1 m, M6 rings and an axial fuse sealed in heat-shrink? Who builds it?
Pins of type Bidirectional and Power output are connected: Symbol U1 Pin 42 [GPIO4, Bidirectional, Line]; Symbol #FLG02 Pin 1 [Power output, Line]
findings.waived_by: designer: The power output is a PWR_FLAG the emitter adds to nets with power inputs and no regulator output: GND_B (U1 GPIO4-9 tied to V- as unused inputs) and ISO_VCC1 (U5 side 1 is powered from MCU pin PB0, <= 4 mA, so the MCU can remove isolator power when no host is present). Neither is a driver conflict.
